===== #10
### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bun workspaces `apps/*` and `packages/*`; `bun install` at the root works; `@kip/shared` and `@kip/server` resolve
- [ ] Root `tsconfig.base.json` (strict), `biome.json`, root scripts `typecheck` (`tsc -b`), `lint`, `test`
- [ ] `apps/server`: Hono `main.api.ts` with `GET /health` returning `{ ok: true }` on `PORT`, an EMPTY tRPC `appRouter` mounted at `/trpc` via `@hono/trpc-server`, and `trpc/init.ts` whose context reads the `x-kip-user` header into `userId`
- [ ] `main.worker.ts` starts node-cron with an empty job list
- [ ] `env.ts` (Zod) and `.env.example` list EVERY variable in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` Env vars, one line each, grouped by feature, optional in development, so no later issue edits them
- [ ] `packages/shared/src/domain/` has stub modules `night-window.ts`, `lnight.ts`, `who-curve.ts`, `spikes.ts`, `attribution.ts`, `construction-hours.ts`, `score-weights.ts`, `wording.ts`, each re-exported from `domain/index.ts`
- [ ] `hq.json`: `setup` = `bun install`; `check` = lint, typecheck, test. CI installs Bun (`oven-sh/setup-bun`) before `./hq setup --ci`
- [ ] `./hq check` passes locally and in CI

### Scope

- `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `tsconfig.base.json`, `biome.json`, `hq.json` (setup and check only)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.env.example`
- `apps/server/` (package.json, tsconfig, `src/main.api.ts`, `src/main.worker.ts`, `src/env.ts`, `src/trpc/`)
- `packages/shared/` (package.json, tsconfig, `src/index.ts`, `src/domain/` stubs)

### Do not touch
===== #11
### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For each of `city`, `night`, `attribution`, `labels`, `briefing`, `evidence`, `stays`, `works`, `live`, `account`: `features/<f>/router.ts` with the procedures from the tRPC routers table (each throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`), `service.ts`, `index.ts`
- [ ] `jobs.ts` (empty list) for `city` and `stays`; `http.ts` for `labels` (`POST /upload/clip`) and `works` (`POST /sns/street-manager`), each returning 501
- [ ] `appRouter` has one line per feature; `main.worker.ts` registers every feature's jobs; `main.api.ts` mounts every http.ts
- [ ] The `AppRouter` type exports from `@kip/server/trpc/router` for the app
- [ ] `./hq check` passes

### Scope

- `apps/server/src/trpc/router.ts`, `apps/server/src/main.api.ts`, `apps/server/src/main.worker.ts`
- `apps/server/src/features/*/` (new stub files only)

### Do not touch
===== #12
### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expo (current SDK) with Expo Router and dev-client config in `apps/mobile`
- [ ] `app/_layout.tsx`: providers (TanStack Query, tRPC client from `src/lib/trpc.ts` using `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` and an `x-kip-user` header generated on first launch and persisted)
- [ ] `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` with tabs City, Night, Stays, Account plus `app/live.tsx`, each rendering a stub screen from `src/features/<f>/screens/`
- [ ] Every feature folder in `src/features/` has `index.ts` and a stub screen
- [ ] `src/lib/ui` primitives (Text, Button, Card, theme tokens) and `src/lib/map`: `Map.web.tsx` (maplibre-gl) and `Map.native.tsx` (`@maplibre/maplibre-react-native`) showing Newcastle (54.973, -1.614) with OSM attribution
- [ ] `app.config.ts`: HealthKit config plugin, microphone, HealthKit and location permission strings, background audio mode
- [ ] Typecheck covers the app; `./hq check` passes

### Scope

- `apps/mobile/` (package.json, app.config.ts, `app/`, `src/lib/`, `src/features/*/` stubs)

### Do not touch
===== #14
### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `night-window.ts`: 23:00 to 07:00 Europe/London, correct across BST changes (`nightOf`, `isInNightWindow`)
- [ ] `lnight.ts`: energy average `10 * log10(mean(10 ^ (L / 10)))`, never an arithmetic mean of dB
- [ ] `who-curve.ts`: `%HSD = 19.4312 - 0.9336 * L + 0.0126 * L^2`; valid 40 to 65 dB, clamped with an `outOfRange` flag outside it, never extrapolated
- [ ] Constant: minimum 30 nights for a city estimate
- [ ] Tests reproduce 2.9% at 45 dB, 6.2% at 55 dB, 8.8% at 60 dB, and a BST-boundary night

### Scope

- `packages/shared/src/domain/night-window.ts`, `lnight.ts`, `who-curve.ts` and their tests

### Do not touch
===== #15
### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `isOutsideRecommendedHours(date)`: allowed Mon to Fri 08:00 to 18:00, Sat 08:00 to 13:00, none on Sundays and England and Wales bank holidays, in Europe/London time
- [ ] Bank holidays snapshotted from `https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json` into a JSON file, with a refresh script
- [ ] Wording constant: "outside the council's recommended hours" (never "illegal")
- [ ] Tests: weekday 06:41 outside, Saturday 13:30 outside, a bank holiday, a BST boundary

### Scope

- `packages/shared/src/domain/construction-hours.ts`, its data file and tests

### Do not touch
===== #18
### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `db/tiger.ts` and `db/mongo.ts` retry on boot with backoff (the Atlas access list lands after the server exists) and never log credentials
- [ ] `db/migrate.ts` applies `db/migrations/*.sql` in filename order with a tracking table; `bun run migrate` at the server
- [ ] `db/indexes.ts` creates every collection and index in the MongoDB table of `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (2dsphere on sensors, hotels, venues, works; nights on userId + startedAt)
- [ ] Unit tests with mocks; Tiger extension check (timescaledb) in the runner

### Scope

- `apps/server/src/db/` (clients, `migrate.ts`, `indexes.ts`, `migrations/` runner only)

### Do not touch
===== #26
### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `infra/`: providers `vultr/vultr` and `mongodb/mongodbatlas` (Tiger provider optional, its URI as a variable)
- [ ] SSH key, private container registry, firewall group (22 from `admin_ip` only; 80 and 443 open), a `vc2-2c-4gb` Ubuntu 24.04 instance in `lhr`, Atlas IP access list for the instance IP

- [ ] `infra/README.md` with apply and `terraform apply -replace=vultr_instance.api`

### Scope

- `infra/`

- [ ] The API serves the web export at `/`; one image runs `main.api.ts` or `main.worker.ts` by command
- [ ] `.dockerignore` excludes `.env*`, `node_modules`, `.context`

def cmd_claim(args):
    cfg = load_config()
    n = args.number
    me = identity(args)
    issue = gh_json(["issue", "view", n, "--json", CLAIM_FIELDS])
    body = issue.get("body") or ""
    refs = blocked_by(body)
    states = dict(zip(refs, pmap(ref_state, refs)))
    for r in refs:
        if states[r] == "UNKNOWN":
            print("%s cannot read blocker #%d; ignoring it" % (WARN, r))
    now = now_utc()
    winner = claim_winner(issue.get("comments"))
    refusals = claim_refusals(n, issue.get("state"), [r for r in refs if states[r] == "OPEN"], winner, me["id"], now)
    if refusals:
        raise Refused(*refusals)

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Infra

Terraform for Kip's server: a Vultr instance in London behind Caddy, its firewall, a private
container registry, and the MongoDB Atlas access entry for the instance's IP. Tiger Cloud is
passed in as a URI. Architecture and the deploy flow: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ("Deploy").

## What it creates
| Resource | Notes |
|---|---|
| `vultr_ssh_key.team` | From `ssh_public_key_path` (default `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`) |
| `vultr_container_registry.kip` | Private, plan `start_up`, in `region` |
| `vultr_firewall_group.api` + rules | 22 from `admin_ip` only; 80 and 443 open for Caddy |
| `vultr_instance.api` | `vc2-2c-4gb`, Ubuntu 24.04 (`os_id` 2284), in `lhr` |
| `mongodbatlas_project_ip_access_list.api` | Allows the instance's IP into Atlas |

`cloud-init.yaml.tftpl` installs Docker, writes `/opt/kip/.env`, a Caddyfile and a compose file,
derives `<ip>.sslip.io` from instance metadata, logs in to the registry and starts the API, the
worker and Caddy. Outputs: `api_ip`, `api_url`, `registry_urn`.

## First apply
1. Credentials in your shell (from 1Password or the MLH emails, never committed):
   `VULTR_API_KEY`, `MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_KEY`, `MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_KEY`.
2. `cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars` and fill it in (git-ignored).
3. Create the registry first, then push the image to it:
   ```bash
   terraform -chdir=infra init
   terraform -chdir=infra apply -target=vultr_container_registry.kip
   terraform -chdir=infra output registry_urn          # e.g. lhr.vultrcr.com/kip
   docker login <registry host>                        # registry credentials from the Vultr console
   docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t <registry_urn>/kip:latest .
   docker push <registry_urn>/kip:latest
   ```
   Set `image = "<registry_urn>/kip:latest"` and the registry credentials in `terraform.tfvars`.
4. `terraform -chdir=infra apply`. Give cloud-init a few minutes, then open `api_url`.

## Ship a new build
```bash
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t <registry_urn>/kip:latest . && docker push <registry_urn>/kip:latest
ssh root@$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw api_ip) 'cd /opt/kip && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d'
```

## Rebuild the server live (demo)
```bash
terraform -chdir=infra plan
terraform -chdir=infra apply -replace=vultr_instance.api
```
This replaces only the instance. Data lives in Atlas and Tiger Cloud, so it stays put; the Atlas
access entry follows the new IP, and the API retries its database connections until it lands.

  for the image address; registry login uses explicit variables because `root_user`'s map keys
  aren't documented in the schema.
EOF

The M0 skeleton in one PR: these nine issues are interlocked (every other M0 issue is blocked on #10), so they ship together.

## What changed
- **#10 workspace:** Bun workspaces, Biome, `tsconfig.base.json`, root `lint`/`typecheck`/`test`; `env.ts` and `.env.example` list every variable from the architecture doc, all optional (blank = unset); domain stub modules under the names in the issue; `hq.json` setup/check; CI installs Bun before `./hq setup --ci`.
- **#11 registries:** every procedure from the routers table, validating input and throwing `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (HTTP 501); `service.ts` per feature, `jobs.ts` for city and stays, `http.ts` for labels and works (501); `AppRouter` at `@kip/server/trpc/router`.
- **#12 app:** Expo SDK 58 + Expo Router + dev client; tabs City, Night, Stays, Account plus Live (and Evidence); an `x-kip-user` ID generated on first launch and persisted; `lib/ui` Text, Button, Card, theme tokens; `lib/map` `Map.web.tsx` (maplibre-gl) and `Map.native.tsx` (MapLibre RN) showing Newcastle with OSM attribution; HealthKit plugin, microphone, HealthKit and location strings, background audio.
- **#14 Lnight/WHO:** `night-window.ts` (`nightOf`, `isInNightWindow`), `lnight.ts`, `who-curve.ts`, 30-night minimum.
- **#15 hours:** `isOutsideRecommendedHours` in London time with a GOV.UK bank-holiday snapshot and `bun run refresh:bank-holidays`; wording constant.
- **#18 databases:** clients with capped exponential backoff that never log errors (which can hold URIs); migration runner with a tracking table and a TimescaleDB check; `ensureIndexes` creates every collection and index; `bun run migrate` / `indexes`.
- **#26 Terraform:** as specified, plus `infra/README.md` (first apply, shipping, `-replace` demo) and a `registry_urn` output.
- **#27 image:** multi-stage Dockerfile; serves the web build and `/health` on 8080; runs the API or the worker by command.
- **#28 night contract:** `NightTimeline` and `NightSummary` with slots for labels, attribution, hours flags, hash and memo; deterministic fixtures (`night-upload.json`, an 8-hour 1 Hz night; `night-timeline.json`) validated by tests.
- Also: `.gitignore` un-ignores `src/lib/` (a global `lib/` rule had hidden the app's lib folder, the cause of the first CI failure).

## How verified
```
$ ./hq check
✓ bun run lint
✓ bun run typecheck
✓ bun run test
✓ 3/3 checks passed
```
- Tests: 32 across shared and server, including both clock-change nights, the 2.9/6.2/8.8% curve points, bank holidays, migrate/indexes with fakes, backoff and no-credential logging, env parsing, stubs answering 501 and user procedures needing `x-kip-user`.
- `bun run apps/server/src/main.api.ts` with no env: `/health` OK, `POST /upload/clip` 501.
- `docker build -t kip .` then `docker run -p <port>:8080 kip` with no env: `/health` OK, the web app at `/` and deep links, `/trpc/city.sensors` 501; the worker starts.
- `expo export --platform web` succeeds, bundling the map with OSM tiles.
- Terraform `fmt -check` and `validate` pass; `urn` and `root_user` confirmed on `vultr_container_registry` in the provider 2.33 schema.
- Anti-slop audit of all UI files: no blur, gradients, shadows, pills or illustrations; solid accent, 1px borders, 6 to 8px radii.

## Deviations from the issues
- Root `typecheck` runs `tsc` in each package rather than `tsc -b`: project references force declaration portability checks that reject the inferred tRPC client types.
- The map component is exported as `MapView` (Biome forbids shadowing the global `Map`); the files are `Map.native.tsx` and `Map.web.tsx` as specified.
- Plain routes are mounted in `app.ts`, which `main.api.ts` serves, so they can be tested without a server.
- Registry login uses explicit Terraform variables: `root_user`'s map keys aren't in the schema.

## Not done here (needs a human)
- `cd apps/mobile && bunx expo start --web` showing the four tabs and the map was not checked in a browser.
- (keys) `bun run migrate` / `indexes` against real `TIGER_URI` / `MONGO_URI`, and `terraform plan`.
- #28: whoever owns phone recording should approve the night contract.

**What I added to close the issues:**

Until #83 merges, make sure nobody dispatches an agent on them. Merging closes all nine automatically.

+## 2026-11-14: Train our own handling-noise filter on a Lium GPU pod
+**Context:** A phone on a nightstand, in a pocket or under a pillow picks up its own handling noise
+(sleeve, pocket, bedsheet rustle). Those spikes would be labelled and linked to wake-ups. We also
+want a model of our own in the pipeline, not only third-party APIs.
+**Decision:** Train a small PyTorch mask model on synthetic mixtures of handling noise and night
+sounds, on a Lium GPU pod (Vultr stays for deployment). Export it to ONNX and run it in the API on
+each spike clip before Gemini. Mostly-handling clips get the label `handling`. Clips are 16 kHz mono
+WAV. Prototype quality is acceptable: if the model underperforms, the API falls back to labelling
+**Consequences:** A Python toolchain (`uv`) beside Bun, outside `./hq check`. Training data and
+checkpoints stay out of git; only the exported model is committed. The label set gains `handling`,
+- **Handling noise** is the phone itself: rubbing on a sleeve, a pocket, a pillow or bedsheets.
+  Kip's own small model (trained by us, see `ml/`) runs on each spike clip before Gemini. A clip
+  that is mostly handling noise is labelled `handling`; otherwise the model's cleaned audio goes on
+  to labelling. `handling` events are never linked to wake-ups and never appear in a briefing.
+- Clips travel as 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV, so the server needs no audio decoder.
- Gemini (paid-tier key) labels each clip, with JSON output. ElevenLabs Scribe audio-event tags
give a second opinion. Where they disagree, the event is `uncertain`. This stops a user's own
snoring being blamed on the building site.

content.content:
---
name: hq-review
description: Use when asked to review someone else's PR ("review PR 12" or "/hq-review 12"). Checks it against the linked issue and sets review:pass or review:changes.
---

# hq-review

Review in your own worktree or workspace, never in the author's. Prefer a reviewer from a
different vendor than the author (the PR's `agent:*` label).

1. Check out the PR: `gh pr checkout <PR>`.
2. Find the issue: `gh pr view <PR> --json title,labels,closingIssuesReferences`, then
   `gh issue view <N>`. Note the Acceptance criteria, Scope and Do not touch.
3. Read the diff: `gh pr diff <PR>`. Flag any file outside Scope or inside Do not touch.
4. Run `./hq check` and the issue's Verify steps.
5. If `command -v claude && command -v codex` succeeds, run `entire review`. It runs Claude Code
   and Codex reviewers plus a judge from the shared profile and posts to the trail. Otherwise
   review by hand against each acceptance criterion.
6. Write the verdict to `.context/review-<PR>.md`:
   - Verdict: pass or changes.
   - Each acceptance criterion: met or not met, with evidence.
   - Findings, blocking first: `file:line`, the problem, a suggested fix.
   - The tail of `./hq check`.
7. Post it: `gh pr review <PR> --comment --body-file .context/review-<PR>.md`.
   Use `--comment`: you cannot approve a PR opened from your own account.
8. Label it:
   - pass: `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass --remove-label review:changes`
   - changes: `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:changes --remove-label review:pass`
9. Do not push fixes to the author's branch and do not merge. Tell the human the verdict.

TimescaleDB won't create a continuous aggregate inside a transaction unless it's `WITH NO DATA`, so the planned `sensor_lnight_daily` migration would stop the API from booting. Fix: a no-transaction marker for such files, or document `WITH NO DATA`.
4. **[Medium] `apps/server/src/db/mongo.ts:9`** — `client.db()` with no name. Atlas connection strings usually have no database path, so everything would land in the `test` database. Fix: `client.db("kip")` or a `MONGO_DB` env variable.
5. **[Low] `.dockerignore:8-9`** — `.env` is only excluded at the root. A `.env` inside `apps/mobile` or `apps/server` would be built into the web bundle or shipped in the image. Fix: add `**/.env*`.
6. **[Low] `apps/server/src/trpc/init.ts:10`** — the `x-kip-user` header isn't checked as a UUID, but `NightUpload.userId` must be one. Fix: validate the header, and check it matches the body's `userId` in `night.upload`. The open CORS is fine because no cookies are used.
7. **[Low] `apps/server/src/retry.ts:28`** (plausible) — the final error keeps the driver error as its cause. If the API crashes, Bun prints that cause chain, which could put a host or username in the logs.
8. **[Low] `hq.json` platform lane `"apps/server/src/*.ts"`** — hq's matching lets `*` cross `/`, so this also matches every feature's server files. Today lane paths are only used for display, so nothing breaks yet.
9. **[Low] `apps/server/src/env.test.ts:19`** — `split("=", 2)` cuts off any value that contains `=`, so the test can pass on a broken value.
10. **[Low] `apps/mobile/src/lib/trpc.ts:9`** — without `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL`, iOS calls a relative `/trpc` that can't resolve. It should fail loudly instead.
11. **[Low] Scope and deviations** — several files fall outside the nine issues' Scope: `README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` contract edits, `compose.yaml`, `bunfig.toml`, `apps/server/src/{app,jobs,http,retry}.ts`, the `hq.json` lane paths, and the shared feature stubs. All fit the platform lane, but the PR body should list them. It should also list three unmet points:
    - #12: four features (attribution, briefing, labels, works) have no stub screen.
    - #27: the image doesn't include `ml/models/`. `ml/` doesn't exist yet, so this probably belongs with #90.
    - `-replace` gives the server a new IP, which breaks the API URL baked into the iOS build. A reserved IP avoids that.

## Acceptance criteria

- **#10, #11, #14, #15, #18:** all met.
  - The listed deviations are reasonable: `tsc` per package instead of `tsc -b`, routes mounted in `app.ts`, and the map named `MapView`.
  - The WHO curve gives 2.934 at 45 dB, 6.198 at 55 dB and 8.775 at 60 dB. The clock-change dates (29 Mar and 25 Oct 2026) and bank holidays, including the 2026-12-28 substitute day, are correct.
- **#12:** met except "every feature folder has a stub screen" (partly met: four have none). Not checked in a browser.
- **#26:** met on paper, but cloud-init is effectively not met because of blocking finding 1.
- **#27:** met except "image includes `ml/models/`". The build wasn't run.
- **#28:** met except the `handling` label (blocking finding 2). Approval by the phone-recording owner is still pending.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Renders cloud-init.yaml.tftpl with sample values (including app_env) and checks it is valid
# YAML with the files cloud-init needs. `terraform validate` can't catch template mistakes.
# Run from infra/ after `terraform init`.
set -euo pipefail
rendered=$(printf '%s\n' 'templatefile("cloud-init.yaml.tftpl", { image = "registry.example/kip/kip:latest", registry_host = "registry.example", registry_user = "user", registry_password = "pass", mongo_uri = "mongodb://m", tiger_uri = "postgres://t", app_env = { GEMINI_API_KEY = "REDACTED", ELEVENLABS_API_KEY = "REDACTED" } })' | terraform console)
printf '%s\n' "$rendered" | sed '1d;$d' | python3 -c '
import sys, yaml
doc = yaml.safe_load(sys.stdin)
files = {f["path"]: f["content"] for f in doc["write_files"]}
env = files["/opt/kip/.env"].splitlines()
assert {"MONGO_URI=mongodb://m", "GEMINI_API_KEY=REDACTED, "ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=REDACTED <= set(env), env
assert "reverse_proxy api:8080" in files["/opt/kip/Caddyfile"]
assert yaml.safe_load(files["/opt/kip/compose.yaml"])["services"].keys() >= {"api", "worker", "caddy"}
print("cloud-init renders to valid YAML with", len(env), "env lines")
'
EOF
chmod +x scripts/check-cloud-init.sh && timeout 150 docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/w -w /w --entrypoint sh hashicorp/terraform:1.13 -c 'apk add -q py3-yaml python3 bash >/dev/null && bash scripts/check-cloud-init.sh' 2>&1 | tail -3
